subject: URGENT: Elevated 5xx/429s and timeouts — suspected retry storm
messages:
From: Suzanne Nguyen <suzanne.nguyen@finpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@finpay.com
Date: 2025-11-02T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: High error rate and timeouts impacting ingestion

Rishi,

We started seeing a major outage at our ingestion layer at ~08:10 PST — we’re observing persistent 5xx and 429 responses from your API and the downstream retries are causing sustained timeouts on our side. Throughput has dropped ~40% and memory on a few of our workers spiked. Attached are a short log extract and a screenshot of the traffic spike.

Key details:
- Errors: ~30% 5xx, 15% 429 at peak
- Timeouts: client-side timeouts after 10s for many requests
- Impact: real-time processing lagging, queued jobs piling up

We need immediate mitigation — can you throttle or put an emergency rule in place? Also want an exec-level contact; this is customer-impacting for our payments flows.

Thanks,
Suzanne
Director, Production Engineering
FinPay

Attachments:
- finpay-logs-20251102.json (excerpt)
- retry-traffic-graph.png (screenshot)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Suzanne Nguyen <suzanne.nguyen@finpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and timeouts impacting ingestion

Suzanne — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. We’re treating this as Sev-1 and I’ve looped in engineering and CS. Initial ask: can you confirm whether you recently rolled any client-side SDK changes or retry logic? Any high-frequency batch jobs started around 08:00?

Immediate actions from our side:
- Engineering (Connor) is pulling detailed ingress metrics and tracing the 429/5xx distribution.
- I’ll put a temporary per-key throttle and enable stricter rate-limits for your API keys to stop downstream retry amplification.
- If helpful, we can flip a server-side proxy rule to return Retry-After headers and enforce exponential backoff for a short window.

I’ll update in 20–30 minutes with the data and next steps. We’ll also prepare an exec summary for your leadership.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and timeouts impacting ingestion — initial findings

On 2025-11-02 09:45 PST I'm seeing the following from our side (summary):

- Traffic trace shows bursty request retries originating from a small set of FinPay IPs/keys between 08:05–08:25.
- Retry pattern: rapid immediate retries (~100–300ms intervals) with 3–5 attempts; no jitter.
- Server-side saturation: several inference hosts hit max concurrent accept queues leading to 503/504 and 429s when token buckets were overdrawn.
- SDK note: FinPay is using an older redwood-js client pinned to 1.2.0 which defaults to linear backoff/no jitter. That lines up with repeated bursts.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:20–09:35):
- Applied short window per-api-key throttles for FinPay (reduce allowed rps by 60%).
- Enabled server-side Retry-After enforcement on the affected routes.
- Deployed temporary circuit-breaker to shed excess request load on saturated hosts.

Effect: 429s and 5xx started to decline after ~09:30. We still see elevated retries in the queue; recommending a few next steps:

Recommended next steps:
1) Ask FinPay to apply exponential backoff + jitter patch (we can provide a hotfix to their SDK).
2) Ship an emergency SDK release that changes default retry behavior (exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts = 2).
3) Long-term: add server-side adaptive throttling and a per-customer burst cap.

Attaching: finpay-logs-20251102.json, retry-traffic-graph.png

— Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and timeouts impacting ingestion — executive escalation

Looping in leadership — this is an exec-level customer impact for FinPay (payments pipeline). Please prepare:
- A 11:00 AM PST bridge with FinPay execs (Rishi, can you confirm?)
- A concise one-slide summary for our CEO and Head of Support (Marissa) with: impact, actions taken, mitigation timeline, and proposed remediation.
- Offer: temporary credits or SLA accommodation if the incident material impact is confirmed.

Connor — prioritize the SDK default change as a hotfix and patch notes. We'll need a comms plan and potential legal touch if we offer credits.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Suzanne Nguyen <suzanne.nguyen@finpay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Postmortem: Retry storm mitigated, follow-up plan

Suzanne — quick summary and next steps following today’s incident: we confirmed a retry storm caused by FinPay client behavior (old SDK defaults + client-side rapid retries) that amplified transient capacity pressure on our inference hosts and produced elevated 5xx/429 rates between ~08:05–09:30 PST.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:20: applied temporary per-key throttles and server-side Retry-After enforcement.
- 09:30: circuit-breaker deployed to shed load on saturated hosts; 5xx/429s began declining.
- 10:00: stabilization confirmed, occasional retries observed but at far lower rates.

Impact: FinPay saw ~40% throughput degradation during the peak window. No data loss; some jobs delayed.

Permanent/near-term actions we’re committing to:
- Emergency SDK hotfix (ETA: 24 hrs): change default retry to exponential backoff with jitter, limit attempts to 2.
- Server-side policy (ETA: 2 weeks): adaptive per-customer burst caps and automatic Retry-After scaling.
- Docs & onboarding (ETA: 1 week): clear guidance on retry behavior and recommended client settings for high-throughput ingestion workloads.
- Joint post-incident review: propose a 30-minute sync with your engineering leads tomorrow at 10:00 PST to walk the technical findings and rollout plan.

We’ve attached the incident postmortem and the logs we used. I’ll arrange the exec bridge for 11:00 and send the calendar invite. If you want us to take additional protective actions (temporary additional rate-limits or throttles longer-term), we can discuss during the bridge.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with the hotfix and updated SDK link when available.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
